key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implant performance depends on integrating implant geometry, biomaterial interfaces, and physiological loading to support durable bone fixation.
engineering_relevance: Design must balance load transfer, micromotion, fatigue resistance, and coating integrity rather than optimize geometry or surface composition alone.
method: Systematic review of implant concepts, biomaterials, and clinical translation.
Synthesis of gait-phase finite element modeling and graded Ti–hydroxyapatite interfaces.
Quantitative trend analysis of evidence maturity and validation depth.
evidence_signal: The analysis covered 34 direct-contribution papers and 32 empirical studies; more than half of the empirical evidence remained at bench or simulation level.
watch_item: Graded Ti–hydroxyapatite evidence came predominantly from non-DWBI analog studies, so DWBI-specific durability and clinical benefit remain unvalidated.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
